name: Maximum Set
description: A set of positive integers $$$S$$$ is called beautiful if, for every two integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ from this set, either $$$x$$$ divides $$$y$$$ or $$$y$$$ divides $$$x$$$ (or both). You are given two integers $$$l$$$ and $$$r$$$. Consider all beautiful sets consisting of integers not less than $$$l$$$ and not greater than $$$r$$$. You have to print two numbers: the maximum possible size of a beautiful set where all elements are from $$$l$$$ to $$$r$$$; the number of beautiful sets consisting of integers from $$$l$$$ to $$$r$$$ with the maximum possible size. Since the second number can be very large, print it modulo $$$998244353$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 2 \cdot 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. Each test case consists of one line containing two integers $$$l$$$ and $$$r$$$ ($$$1 \le l \le r \le 10^6$$$).
output_specification: For each test case, print two integers — the maximum possible size of a beautiful set consisting of integers from $$$l$$$ to $$$r$$$, and the number of such sets with maximum possible size. Since the second number can be very large, print it modulo $$$998244353$$$.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1796C — Maximum Set [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
